Hi Sarah — looping in Kimberly (Insurance & Legal) and Laura (Contracts ops) to review the naming and endorsement ask.

Quick context for your team: Redwood's standard position is to provide a COI plus an endorsement naming the customer as Additional Insured for GL and Waiver of Subrogation where carriers permit. We generally do not accept retroactive dates unless negotiated with underwriting (can cause carrier resistance).

Kimberly — can you review HelioSys's draft order form and current COI and confirm:
1) whether the endorsement HelioSys requests is compatible with Redwood's insurer panel or requires an insurer-specific endorsement;
2) if we can commit to waiver of subrogation on this program; and
3) an estimated turnaround for a revised COI + endorsement once we provide the exact naming string.

Laura — I'll need a checklist to pass to HelioSys for procurement. I started one (attached) — please add any items I missed.

Target: provide a formal answer and (if possible) insurer/ broker contact by EOD 2027-11-05 to keep HelioSys on their signature timeline.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: MSA/order form — insurance evidence and naming

Hi all — reviewed the draft Order Form and HelioSys COI. A few notes and suggested redlines:

- Coverage minimums: Redwood can confirm the GL and Professional Liability limits as stated (GL 1M/2M, E&O 1M) but we need to flag auto liability limits if HelioSys requires hired/non-owned auto coverage.
- Additional Insured: we can issue an endorsement naming "HelioSys Inc., its subsidiaries and affiliates" — we need the exact legal entity name(s) for the parent/legal entity HelioSys intends to name. If they want a specific subsidiary named, provide the full legal name and address.
- Waiver of Subrogation: carriers vary; we can request it but cannot guarantee until binder/underwriter sign-off. If HelioSys requires a firm commitment, we should confirm if a temporary waiver is acceptable or an underwriting-approved waiver is necessary.
- Retroactive date: we do not generally accept retroactive dating on endorsements for professional liability policies without insurer approval — expect underwriting review and potential surcharge.

I attached our standard endorsement template and marked places where HelioSys's wording conflicts with carrier-accepted language.

Action items:
1) HelioSys to confirm exact naming/addresses for additional insured.
2) Broker (Tom Garrison at InsureCo) to confirm if current carriers will issue a waiver of subrogation and provide timeline for amended COI + endorsement.
3) Legal/Contracts (Laura) to accept the minor redlines or escalate any commercial asks.

Estimated ETA: if broker confirms today, we can issue a revised COI + endorsement within 3 business days (subject to insurer lead times).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Insurance & Risk Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: RW_Endorsement_Template.pdf (pdf)
From: Tom Garrison <tom.g@insureco.com>
To: kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com, david.kim@redwoodinference.com

Date: Sat, 6 Nov 2027 10:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MSA/order form — insurance evidence and naming

Hi Kimberly / David / Sarah,

We reviewed the current policies on Redwood's program. We can provide a revised COI and an Additional Insured endorsement for GL. For E&O/Professional Liability, many carriers will issue a statement of coverage but not a traditional AI endorsement; we can provide an alternative form (insurer confirmation letter) if HelioSys requires it.

On Waiver of Subrogation: we can request it from the carrier. Most will grant it for sovereign entities and many corporate purchasers, but a small subset of carriers may decline. If HelioSys requires a binding waiver, that may extend underwriting review by 5–7 business days.

We need two things from Redwood to proceed:
- Exact naming string for the Additional Insured as it should appear on the endorsement (legal entity + address).
- Confirmation whether HelioSys requires the parent company included or just the contracting entity.

Turnaround estimate: 48–72 hours for COI + standard AI endorsement once we have the naming string; 5–7 business days if underwriting needs to approve waiver of subrogation or retroactive date changes.

Regards,
Tom Garrison
Senior VP, Commercial Lines
InsureCo Brokerage
